sources.name: ODN height — EPSG:5701
verified_facts: EPSG:5701 is a valid vertical coordinate reference system named ODN height.
Its scope includes geodesy and engineering survey.
The registry records Newlyn height as an alias and Ordnance Survey of Great Britain as the information source.
semantic_limits: A valid vertical CRS identifier does not prove that a raster cell contains ODN height values.
CRS identity, source accuracy, pixel validity and parcel geometry binding remain separate checks.

sources.name: National Geoid Model OSGM15
verified_facts: OSGM15 provides a vertical transformation between ETRS89 ellipsoidal height and orthometric height.
In mainland Britain it returns Ordnance Datum Newlyn heights.
The model uses a 1 kilometre grid with bilinear interpolation and states nominal mainland accuracy of 8 millimetres RMS.
semantic_limits: OSGM15 transformation accuracy is not Environment Agency LiDAR vertical accuracy.
A geoid transformation does not prove parcel min/max values or exact source-pixel provenance.

sources.name: ETRS89-GBR to ODN height (2) — EPSG:7711
verified_facts: EPSG:7711 is a valid transformation from ETRS89-GBR OSNet v2009 to ODN height.
The registry gives an accuracy value of 0.008 metres and a scope of deriving gravity-related heights from GNSS observations.
It uses the OSGM15 geoid correction model and supersedes the older OSGM02-based transformation.
semantic_limits: The registry accuracy applies to the coordinate transformation, not terrain-model measurement.
EPSG:7711 must not be used to upgrade the confidence of LiDAR cells or HMLR polygon boundaries.

sources.name: OGC Features and Geometries JSON Part 1: Core
verified_facts: JSON-FG extends GeoJSON with mandatory support for coordinate reference systems other than WGS 84 longitude/latitude.
It requires a declaration of the JSON-FG conformance classes used by an encoded feature or feature collection.
Where a geometry can be represented as GeoJSON, the geographic feature geometry is encoded as a GeoJSON object.
semantic_limits: Declaring a native CRS in JSON transport does not establish geometry validity or legal-boundary accuracy.
Exact parcel containment still requires the authoritative native EPSG:27700 polygon and independent topology checks.
